To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present an unsupervised variational approach to learning view-invariant object representations from videos.
we introduce a new unsupervised model, SIMON, that is capable of learning to disentangle and represent object attributes in a view-invariant manner.

SIMONe: (i) learns to infer object-level and frame-level latent representations from video alone, (ii) represents object attributes in an object-centric manner that does not depend on the agent’s view, and (iii) can disentangle and abstract object dynamics in order to summarize their trajectories in a view-invariant manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning to represent and reason about the compositional structure in a given scene, in particular the configuration and properties of objects comprising the environment.

developing a new approach to unsupervised representation learning for videos, which is able to learn a view-invariant and temporally-abstracted representation for the objects in the video, and to use it for a variety of downstream tasks such as video synthesis and segmentation.
learning to represent and reason about objects, their attributes, and their interactions in the real world.

SIMONe learns to infer two types of latent representations from video input: object latents that represent the object-level contents of a scene, as well the global time-varyings elements such as viewpoint, allowing our model to represent object attributes that are not viewpoint-dependent, as well as time-abstracting the dynamics of objects, summarizing their trajectory as time-abstract properties.
the paper presents a novel unsupervised approach for learning view-invariant, time-abstracted object representations from video.

SIMONe learns to represent the time-invariant and view-invariant object-level structure of scenes, and is able to disentangle and summarize the time-varying dynamics of objects in a manner that allows for view-invariant object tracking and instance segmentation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a model that is capable of learning a representation for the objects in a scene, which is invariant to viewpoint and time.
SIMONe can learn a set of object-level latent variables which are invariant to viewpoint and time, and can be used to reconstruct a scene in novel viewpoints.
we propose a novel unsupervised model that can learn object representations that are invariant to viewpoint.

we can learn a model that can represent objects in an allocentric, view-invariant manner from RGB videos.
the same video can be used to train two different latent spaces, one that captures object dynamics and another that captures the viewpoint.
